### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. microcephalic osteodysplastic primordial dwarfism type I  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.790)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:34016)

**Proposed mechanism:** RNU4ATAC (HGNC:14240) —DISRUPTS→ U12-dependent spliceosome assembly and function (GO:0005681); U12-dependent spliceosome assembly and function (GO:0005681) —LEADS_TO→ Microcephaly (HP:0000252); U12-dependent spliceosome assembly and function (GO:0005681) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal dysplasia (HP:0002650); U12-dependent spliceosome assembly and function (GO:0005681) —LEADS_TO→ Primordial dwarfism (HP:0005854). Mutations in RNU4ATAC disrupt the U12-dependent spliceosome, leading to impaired pre-mRNA splicing. This disruption affects the expression of numerous genes critical for development, ultimately manifesting as microcephaly, skeletal dysplasia, and primordial dwarfism in both Lowry-Wood syndrome and microcephalic osteodysplastic primordial dwarfism type I.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of distinct, non-overlapping sets of genes or pathways significantly dysregulated in Lowry-Wood syndrome versus microcephalic osteodysplastic primordial dwarfism type I, despite both being linked to RNU4ATAC mutations, would challenge this hypothesis. Furthermore, if specific variants in RNU4ATAC were found to consistently segregate with one phenotype but not the other, this would refine the mechanistic link. _(variant: The absence of common pathogenic variants in RNU4ATAC in the general population (gnomAD))_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of RNU4ATAC and the U12-dependent spliceosome in these distinct primordial dwarfism syndromes could reveal common therapeutic targets or strategies for modulating splicing defects to ameliorate developmental outcomes.
